newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The new index-linked state bond will be issued next month, according to Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis. He said that the bond - supported by an inflation clause - will range in interest from 12.4 percent (seven-year bond) and 10.2 percent (three-year bonds).
--Some 20 Athens stock exchange firms have been summoned by the Capital Market Commission to to make a deposition regarding the vioation of bourse legislation revealed in a recent audit.

--The president of Ethniki Securities Nikos Karamouzis yesterday announced measures to avert insider trading and the significant participation of the Hellenic Industrial and Development Bank (ETEBA) in Ethnikis's share capital within 1997 and alliances with houses from abroad.

--The government hopes to cull 150 billion drachmas from outstanding court debts. An amendment submitted to Parliament yesterday authorises the tax department to chase payment for fines for misdemenours such as illegal construction, or driving offences.
IMERISIA
--The Greek economy will find itself in new surroundings in 1997 as new conditions are shaped in Europe and even greater efforts will be needed to push down inflation, unemployment and deficits.
--An OECD delegation is in town to conduct a feasibility study on the insurance system.
--Next week will see the presentation of a new bill in Parliament governing procedures for public tenders.
KERDOS
--The National Bank of Greece is studying alternative proposals which will allow its expansion. Sources say these include not paying a dividend but providing shareholders with shares instead.
--The first 10 days of February will see the announcement for the appointment of an adviser for the public fuel company's (DEP) floatation on the stock exchange.
EXPRESS

--Public spending will be under the microscope and the government's policy of fiscal discipline will be imposed, Deputy Finance Minister Christodoulakis says at yesterday's meeting of all ministry economic directors.
--Incomes will be index-linked as of 1997 and there will be an increase in the tax-free threshold, the finance ministry promised unionists after a meeting yesterday.
--The development ministry yesterday withdraw the operating licence for Peiraiki Insurance and another three are expected to be shut down by the end of February.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The economy gets some relief as the tension on ports dies down and farmers receive improved proposals.
--The environment, town planning and public works ministry is promoting a plan to systemise the procedure for placing public works projects. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
